name: Telescope Array (Utah): surface-detector array, fluorescence stations and laser
notes: All 507 surface-detector stations are drawn from TASDPosition.dat in the Telescope Array Collaboration data release on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8405760, CC BY 4.0), in 7 west-to-east strips of 72 or 73 as 1.73 m markers (the contract allows no MultiPoint). The release states no origin or orientation; the frame (origin at the CLF, axes true east and north) was found by registering the table against Fig. 5 of arXiv:2103.01086, a plot on latitude and longitude axes: median residual 14 m, rotation -0.001 deg. Accuracy 100 m.

The three fluorescence stations (Black Rock Mesa, Long Ridge, Middle Drum) are read from the triangle markers of Fig. 1 of arXiv:1410.3151 registered to the station table, so each is good to about 500 m and is a figure reading, not a published coordinate. No document fetched gives their latitude and longitude. The three are 20.8 km from the CLF, which the papers describe as equidistant from all three, about 21 km.

The previous version drew one 6 km-precision point (geometry:ta-array-point) at the centre quoted as "39.3 N and 112.9 W" in arXiv:1201.4964; it is removed because the stations and the laser now carry the location. The old worklog said telescopearray.org was unreachable; its address now redirects to a dynamic-DNS host that was not followed.
TAx4 (500 further stations at 2.08 km spacing, arXiv:2103.01086) is not drawn: its positions are published only as a figure of deployed and planned locations.
The array is a square 1.2 km grid of 507 stations, whose centroid is 4.0 km south of the CLF; the CLF is the centre of the three-telescope triangle.

summary.plain: The Telescope Array cosmic-ray observatory in the Utah desert: all 507 scintillator stations on their 1.2 km grid, the outline of the array, the central laser, and the three fluorescence telescope stations that overlook the array from three sides.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:telescope-array-utah. The 507 SD stations are the x, y columns of TASDPosition.dat (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.8405760), placed with the origin at the Central Laser Facility (39.296918 N, 112.908733 W from arXiv:1410.3151) and axes true east and north, a frame established by registration against a published latitude-longitude plot (median residual 14 m). The three FD stations are read from a published layout figure registered to the table (accuracy 500 m). TAx4 is not drawn.
